title: EVerest federated testing metadata contract (OpenHTF)
description: Contract for TestRecord.metadata in an EVerest federated testing submission. OpenHTF is the normalised internal format here, and it models a device under test - it has no concept of a source commit, a build, or a test suite. Everything that identifies WHAT was tested therefore lives here, in an untyped metadata object, which is the same closed-schema problem CTRF had with results.extra, moved to a different field. This file is what gives it meaning.

everest.description: What was tested. OpenHTF has no native field for any of this.

commit.description: FULL 40-character EVerest commit SHA. With tags replaced by force-pushed pointer branches this is the ONLY durable identifier a submission carries, so a short SHA is rejected.

pointer.description: The floating pointer branch that was tracked.

tracks.description: The real branch the pointer follows, e.g. main or stable/2026.02.

testEnvironment.description: Simulation or real hardware. Displayed separately, so exactly these two.

buildUrl.description: Link back to the run. Optional but strongly encouraged - with attachments capped it is the only route to full detail.

build.description: Build status. OpenHTF has no build concept either, so it lives here. The intake gate rejects a submission whose build is missing or failed.

modules.description: EVerest modules built. Required: without it a submission cannot say which parts of EVerest it actually exercised, so two passing runs covering different module sets look identical. Checked against schema/everest-modules.txt and warned on if unknown.

id.description: Unique integrator id. Also the results/<id>/ directory name. Use a pseudonym to stay anonymous; there is no separate publication flag because the repository is public.

hardware.description: Board-level detail. Per-DUT identity belongs in OpenHTF's native dut_id and station_id, not here.

bsp.description: Board support package or firmware identifier for the board itself, e.g. yeti-fw-1.4.2. NOT an EVerest module name - the modules a run exercised go in build.modules.

board.description: Board MODEL, e.g. yeti-1.1. This is the closest thing CTRF has to a device identity, and it is a model rather than a rig: two rigs with the same board are indistinguishable in a CTRF submission. Required when testEnvironment is HIL.

chargeController.description: Charge controller model or firmware, if it is a separate unit from the board.

source.description: Set by the normaliser when a submission arrived as CTRF and was converted, so the provenance of a converted record is never lost.

archived.description: Set by scripts/archive.py when the record was archived and its traces, attachments and codeinfo stripped. Present so an archived record still validates, and so a reader can tell a record with no attachments from one whose attachments were dropped.

synthesised.description: Fields on this record that normalise.py manufactured because the submitted format has no equivalent - dut_id and station_id on the CTRF path. A reader must be able to tell a synthesised value from a reported one.
